statusHistory.note: From the Berlin (deep) war-room slate, verified independently rather than trusting the queue note. Founding confirmed via own site and German Wikipedia: opened 12 November 1978 at Bülowstraße 17 as 'Prinz Eisenherz,' founded by Peter Hedenström, Lothar Lang, Michael Keim and Christian von Maltzahn out of West Berlin's gay liberation and left student movements — making it Germany's first gay bookshop and one of Europe's oldest surviving. Moves confirmed: Bülowstraße 17 (1978-mid-1980s) to Bleibtreustraße 52, Charlottenburg (mid-1980s-2004) to Lietzenburger Straße 9a, Schöneberg (2004-2013) to current Motzstraße 23, Schöneberg (since November 2013). Name dropped 'Prinz' as the shop expanded lesbian and trans stock. Currently trading: own site confirms address and ongoing exhibition/reading programming; hero photo is the current Motzstraße storefront. Cross-city link: a genuine reciprocal thread with Gay's the Word (London, opened Jan 1979) exists — both are pre-1980, still-independent queer bookshops that survived a hostile-state era and are drafted within a year of each other; link added both ways.
